title: Orsen and the Salt
premise: Petra Joubert maps the unmapped from a valley where magic cannot follow, hiding the gift they inherited from a mother burned for it. When the crown's witch-hunt reaches the valley, Petra flees with Orsen, a salt-scarred ex-soldier who once served the hunters, and discovers their gift is tied to the last living dragon's failing flame. Pursued by Inquisitor Hale, Petra must choose between destroying their magic to stay safe or feeding the dragon's fire with memories of everyone they love. In the end, Petra gives up their mother's memory—not their own—to reignite the dragon-fire, ending the hunt and choosing Orsen over the duty of inheritance.
about_author: Mara Nystrom is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing forgotten maps before turning to fiction. She writes from a coastal town where the fog, she insists, is doing most of the storytelling.

chapters.title: The Valley That Forgets
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. We meet Petra mapping the valley's edge, where their compass spins uselessly and magic cannot follow. A quiet chapter establishing their hidden gift, inherited from an executed mother, and their careful invisible life. Emotional beat: the loneliness of a secret kept so long it has become a personality.

chapters.title: Proclamation at the Mill
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. The crown's criers announce a realm-wide hunt for the gifted; neighbors begin watching neighbors. Petra burns their mother's letters but keeps one page by accident. Emotional beat: fear curdling into defiance as Petra realizes invisibility was always someone else's promise, never theirs.

chapters.title: Orsen at the Gate
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. A scarred stranger arrives seeking a guide past the valley wards—Orsen, a deserter from the Inquisition who knows what the hunt really wants. He recognizes what Petra is and says nothing. Emotional beat: two people recognizing each other's masks before either admits wearing one.

chapters.title: What the Wards Keep Out
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Inquisitor Hale enters the valley with a salt-iron cage that nullifies wards. Petra and Orsen flee through the pass Petra alone has mapped, and outside the valley Petra's gift ignites for the first time—the land answering them. Emotional beat: terror and wonder braided together at first contact with real magic.

chapters.title: Salt Roads
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. On the road, Orsen confesses he helped cage gifted children before deserting; Petra must decide if love can survive complicity. They follow Petra's instinctive pull toward something ancient calling through the mountains. Emotional beat: trust built in the space between confession and forgiveness.

chapters.title: The Guttering
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. They find the last dragon, Vess, dying in a caldera, her flame kept alive only by stored memories of the gifted dead—including, Petra realizes, their mother's. The hunt isn't for prisoners; it's for fuel. Emotional beat: grief discovering it has been weaponized.

chapters.title: Hale's Bargain
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Hale corners them, offering Orsen full pardon if he delivers Petra; she reveals the war the dragon-fire once ended will resume if Vess dies. Duty, mercy, and survival stop pointing the same direction. Emotional beat: Orsen choosing, finally, whose side history will say he stood on.

chapters.title: Memory Is a Currency
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Vess explains the choice: feed the flame with memories, each one gone forever. Petra begins giving small ones—a taste, a song—and feels themselves thinning while the fire brightens. Emotional beat: the horror of learning exactly how much of yourself you are willing to spend.

chapters.title: The Last Dragon-Fire
chapters.summary: Climax, alternating POV. Hale attacks the caldera as Petra makes the final offering: not their own memories, but their mother's preserved page, breaking inheritance itself to end the cycle. Vess blazes back to life; the hunt collapses without its purpose. Emotional beat: sacrifice reframed—not losing yourself, but refusing to lose yourself.

chapters.title: A Map With No Edges
chapters.summary: Petra's POV, epilogue-like. Months later, Petra draws the first honest map of the realm, wards dissolved, dragons known, magic free. Orsen builds them a house on no border at all. Emotional beat: quiet joy—an ending defined not by what was given up, but by what was finally allowed to be kept.
